newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Pacific Ports to offer 200 mln shrs in flotation.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Ports to offer 200 mln shrs in flotation.

text.p: Pacific Ports Co Ltd, the port operating arm of Fairyoung Holdings Ltd, said on Monday it was offering 200 million shares at HK$3.09 each in a share flotation.

The company said about 160 million shares would be placed with institutional and professional investors and 40 million shares would be opened for an initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong from April 15 to 18.
The firm has granted underwriters an overallotment option to require issue of up to another 30 million new shares.
The issue price represents a prospective price/earnings multiple of 42.3 times on a proforma fully-diluted basis and 45.4 times on a weighted average basis, the company said.
Dealing in the shares is expected to begin on April 25. Peregrine Capital Ltd is the global coordinator of the issue.
Pacific Ports is engaged in investment, development, operation and management of seaport and riverport terminals.
Currently, the company holds the development rights of over five port infrastructure projects in Xiamen in China's Fujian Province, and in Nanjing and Suzhou in Jiangsu province.
The company said it is also exploring other port investment opportunities throughout Asia.

Pacific Ports said the net proceeds from the share issue would be about HK$583 million, of which HK$460 million would be used for the construction of and equipment purchases for its port projects in China over the next three years.
The rest would be used as working capital.
The company said net tangible assets per share is HK$3.64 and its prospective annual dividend yield is 0.97 percent.
It forecast a net profit, before extraordinary items, of not less than HK$50 million for the year to December 31, 1997.
The company estimates a combined loss, after taxation and minority interests but before extraordinary items, of not less than HK$17 million for 1996.
It quotes a loss attributable to shareholders of HK$11.23 million for 1995, and of HK$3.29 million for 1994.
